notes: Responder/non-responder subtype | Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: Feasibility of immersive 40 Hz gamma sensory stimulation in early-stage Alzheimer's disease
journal: The Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease
method: Single-session within-subject sham-controlled VR audiovisual 40 Hz; EEG; memory
data: Human (n=11 MCI due to AD or mild AD); audiovisual VR
key_finding: Safe; stronger 40 Hz EEG response than baseline and sham; exploratory better recall for items encoded during 40 Hz
limitation: Single session, n=11
notes: Pilot in healthy older adults: Reis 2025 Sci Rep 10.1038/s41598-025-13725-6 | Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: The safety and efficacy of gamma frequency auditory and visual stimulation in the treatment of alzheimer's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis
method: Systematic review and meta-analysis of controlled trials to Nov 2025
key_finding: Safe overall (tinnitus risk higher); structural brain measures improved but NO significant effect on cognition (SMD 0.16, P=0.55) or ADL
limitation: High heterogeneity; many small sponsor-linked trials
notes: Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: Efficacy of auditory gamma stimulation for cognitive decline: a systematic review of individual and group differences across cognitively impaired and healthy populations
method: Systematic review (62 studies)
key_finding: Animal findings on amyloid clearance and neuroinflammation not consistently replicated in humans; neurophysiological response did not reliably predict benefit; 32 different neurophysiological measures used
limitation: Review
notes: Supports auditory-only gap statements | Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: Exposure to gamma tACS in Alzheimer's disease: A randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled, crossover, pilot study
method: Single 60 min 40 Hz tACS over Pz vs sham; crossover; TMS SAI (cholinergic)
key_finding: Improved RAVLT recall after one gamma tACS session; cholinergic marker modulated
limitation: Single session; acute memory effect
notes: Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: Increasing Brain Gamma Activity Improves Episodic Memory and Restores Cholinergic Dysfunction in Alzheimer's Disease
method: Single 60 min gamma tACS over precuneus vs sham; crossover; EEG in subset
key_finding: Improved RAVLT immediate/delayed recall and face-name associations vs sham; SAI restored
limitation: Single session
notes: Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: Impact of 40 Hz Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation on Cerebral Tau Burden in Patients with Alzheimer's Disease: A Case Series
method: 1 h/day 40 Hz bitemporal tACS for 4 weeks; PiB, FTP (tau) and PBR28 (microglia) PET
key_finding: p-tau PET fell >2% in 3/4 patients in targeted temporal regions; EEG gamma power increased
limitation: n=4, no control
notes: MGH/Santarnecchi group (NCT03880240 family) | Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: Impact of multisession 40Hz tACS on hippocampal perfusion in patients with Alzheimer's disease
method: 40 Hz tACS 1 h/day for 2-4 weeks, temporal lobe; ASL MRI
key_finding: Increased bilateral temporal perfusion; correlated with episodic memory change
limitation: Open-label
notes: Vascular mechanism parallel to M22 | Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: Gamma neuromodulation improves episodic memory and its associated network in amnestic mild cognitive impairment: a pilot study
method: Eight 60 min 40 Hz tACS sessions; memory; plasma AD biomarkers; RSFC
key_finding: Memory improved; NO change in plasma AD biomarkers
limitation: Open-label pilot
notes: Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: Home-Based Gamma Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation in Patients With Alzheimer Disease: A Randomized Clinical Trial
method: Double-blind sham-controlled 8 weeks home gamma tACS over precuneus (5x/week) + 8 weeks open-label
key_finding: Significant benefit on CDR-SB, ADAS-Cog, ADCS-ADL and face-name test vs sham; gamma power and cholinergic markers increased; no plasma biomarker change
limitation: Single centre; short duration; small absolute effects
notes: NCT05643326 (tACS@Home). Crossref title omits the subtitle 'A Randomized Clinical Trial' that PubMed shows | Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: 40 Hz biparietal transcranial alternating current stimulation for Alzheimer's disease: a prospective study
method: Randomized tACS vs sham, 15 days x 30 min biparietal; TMS-EEG; fMRI; 10-week follow-up
data: Human (mild AD; n per full text); tACS
key_finding: Improved global cognition and several domains; increased DMN connectivity
limitation: Retrospectively registered; single centre
notes: Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: 40-Hz steady state response in Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment
method: EEG 40 Hz auditory click-train SSR; 1-week test-retest
data: Human (15 mild AD, 20 MCI, 20 controls); auditory
key_finding: 40 Hz SSR power INCREASED in AD vs MCI and controls; high test-retest reliability; correlated with ADAS-cog
limitation: Small; drug-naive but mild AD only
notes: Contradicts assumption that AD brains cannot generate 40 Hz responses | Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: Enhanced magnetic auditory steady-state response in early Alzheimer's disease
method: MEG 40 Hz monaural ASSR; dipole modelling
data: Human (mild-moderate AD vs age-matched controls); auditory
key_finding: ASSR significantly INCREASED in AD; interpreted as reduced inhibition
limitation: Small; older methods
notes: Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: Effect of Mild Cognitive Impairment and Alzheimer Disease on Auditory Steady-State Responses
method: ASSR thresholds at 40 and 80 Hz modulation, 500-2000 Hz carriers
key_finding: Normal 40 vs 80 Hz threshold differences were largely lost in MCI and absent in AD
limitation: Threshold (audiological) measure, not amplitude/phase-locking; small
notes: Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: Synchrony in auditory 40-Hz gamma oscillations increases in older age and correlates with hearing abilities and cortical GABA levels
method: MEG 40 Hz ASSR in quiet and babble noise; MRS GABA
key_finding: 40 Hz ASSR amplitude increased in older adults; larger ASSR in noise linked to worse hearing; related to auditory cortex GABA
limitation: Healthy aging only; no AD
notes: Shows aging itself raises ASSR - confound for AD comparisons | Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: Developmental and aging trajectories of 40-Hz auditory steady-state responses: A systematic review across the human lifespan
method: Systematic review (40 studies)
key_finding: In adulthood/aging, findings heterogeneous (preserved, diminished or enhanced 40 Hz synchronization); sparse older-adult and longitudinal data
limitation: Review
notes: Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: Auditory steady state response can predict declining EF in healthy elderly individuals
method: Longitudinal 40 Hz ASSR + cognition in Metropolit Birth Cohort; GLM; vision transformer
key_finding: Individuals with declining cognition had larger area of entrainment and delayed ASSR assembly; associated with poorer executive function
limitation: Not AD-diagnosed; single cohort
notes: Again, 'more' ASSR tracks decline | Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: Stimulus-induced gamma rhythms are weaker in human elderly with mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease
method: EEG during large gratings (induced gamma) and SSVEP
key_finding: Stimulus-induced (native) gamma lower in MCI/AD, but steady-state visual evoked responses were NOT different
limitation: Very small MCI/AD groups
notes: Native gamma vs driven steady-state response dissociate - central to D01 argument | Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: The bidirectional effect of attention on gamma sensory stimulation: 40 Hz entrainment is weakened by externally-induced distraction but enhanced by internally-induced distraction
method: EEG 40 Hz entrainment under attention/distraction manipulations
data: Human (sample size per full text); auditory 40 Hz clicks
key_finding: 40 Hz ASSR strong when attending, even stronger with internal (mind-wandering) distraction, minimal when a podcast competed with the clicks
limitation: Healthy participants; small sample per authors
notes: Relevant to D05 task effect and to home-use designs that add audio content; other agent covers measurement | Crossref title/year/journal + PubMed PMID matched 2026-09-30

title: Measuring phase synchrony in brain signals
method: Phase-locking value (PLV): consistency of the phase difference between two signals across trials, with surrogate statistics
key_finding: Introduced PLV to quantify inter-site phase synchrony separately from amplitude
limitation: Inflated by volume conduction/common reference and by a shared driven input; biased upward with few trials
relevance_to_project: ds005048's paper (DAT01) reports inter-site PLV during 40 Hz sound; a common 40 Hz evoked source seen at many electrodes can raise PLV without any real interaction between areas

title: Phase lag index: Assessment of functional connectivity from multi channel EEG and MEG with diminished bias from common sources
method: Phase lag index (PLI): asymmetry of the phase-difference distribution; ignores zero-lag coupling
data: Coupled-oscillator model; EEG absence seizure; EEG 15 AD vs 13 controls; 2 MEG sets
key_finding: PLI much less affected by common sources/reference than phase coherence; detected beta-band connectivity changes in AD
limitation: Discards true zero-lag coupling; discontinuous near 0/pi; biased by noise and sample size (fixed by wPLI, MEA03)
relevance_to_project: Lag-insensitive alternative to PLV for 40 Hz connectivity claims in dementia EEG

title: An improved index of phase-synchronization for electrophysiological data in the presence of volume-conduction, noise and sample-size bias
method: Weighted PLI (wPLI) and debiased wPLI estimator
key_finding: wPLI weights by imaginary cross-spectrum magnitude, reducing noise sensitivity and sample-size bias vs PLI/ImC
limitation: Still blind to zero-lag interactions; needs enough trials; source leakage partly persists
relevance_to_project: Recommended connectivity metric to re-test the 'frontal-parietal PLV increase' in DAT01 without volume-conduction inflation

title: Stimulus Specificity of Phase-Locked and Non-Phase-Locked 40 Hz Visual Responses in Human
method: Time-frequency split into phase-locked (evoked) vs non-phase-locked (induced) gamma
data: Human EEG, n=8, visual illusory-triangle task
key_finding: Evoked (~40 Hz, ~100 ms) and induced (~280 ms) gamma behave differently across stimuli
limitation: Visual, young adults, transient not steady-state stimulation
relevance_to_project: Basis for splitting the 40 Hz response into evoked power (average first) vs total/induced power (single-trial first); PAC or 'entrainment' measured on total power mixes the two

title: On the statistical significance of electrophysiological steady-state responses
method: Significance of steady-state responses: SNR against noise estimated from the two neighboring spectral lines
data: Analytical derivation for ERG/PERG/VEP steady-state recordings
key_finding: Noise estimated from neighboring bins is far more sensitive than a separate no-stimulus recording (5% significance at SNR 2.82 vs 4.36)
limitation: Assumes a smooth noise spectrum near the response frequency; the 1/f slope and line noise break this
relevance_to_project: Gives a principled 40 Hz SNR vs neighboring-bin test for per-window/per-subject entrainment detection; bias from 1/f slope in older adults should be checked (MEA07)

title: The Caveats of observing Inter-Trial Phase-Coherence in Cognitive Neuroscience
method: Simulations of how power changes and evoked responses affect inter-trial phase coherence (ITPC)
key_finding: Apparent ITPC changes can happen with no real change in ongoing phase, caused by power changes or overlapping evoked responses
limitation: Simulation-only; focused on alpha and pre-stimulus phase
relevance_to_project: ITPC/phase-locking to 40 Hz sound cannot by itself separate 'entrained oscillator' from 'repeated evoked response'

title: Parameterizing neural power spectra into periodic and aperiodic components
method: FOOOF/specparam: fits the power spectrum as an aperiodic 1/f part plus Gaussian peaks
data: Simulations + human EEG/MEG/LFP (incl. aging working-memory data)
key_finding: Band power conflates periodic and aperiodic changes; the aperiodic exponent/offset change with age and state
limitation: Peak fitting is fragile when a narrow driven 40 Hz line sits on a broad spectrum; settings affect results
relevance_to_project: Needed to express 40 Hz SNR relative to the individual aperiodic background, because older/dementia EEG has a different 1/f slope

title: Stimulus Induced Desynchronization of Human Auditory 40-Hz Steady-State Responses
method: MEG 40 Hz ASSR (500 Hz tone, 40 Hz AM) with a concurrent contralateral noise burst
key_finding: Noise burst cut ASSR amplitude for ~250 ms, longer than the burst's own gamma response, so linear superposition cannot explain it; the ASSR then built up again as after onset
limitation: Young adults only; MEG; one type of perturbation
relevance_to_project: Rare direct evidence for 40 Hz AUDITORY that the ASSR has a nonlinear, resettable (oscillator-like) part; a perturbation/reset test not yet repeated in older adults or dementia
notes: Categorized here as entrainment_vs_evoked (measurement paradigm)

title: Measuring Phase-Amplitude Coupling Between Neuronal Oscillations of Different Frequencies
method: Modulation index (MI): KL divergence of the phase-binned amplitude distribution from uniform
key_finding: MI is a robust PAC measure that detects multimodal coupling; the paper sets out filtering and surrogate practice
limitation: Needs long data; biased for short windows; cannot tell true coupling from waveform-shape effects
relevance_to_project: The project's PAC 'forecast' uses Tort MI in 2 s windows (theta phase x 38-42 Hz amplitude); see PAC03/PAC07/PAC08 for why this is questionable

title: Untangling cross-frequency coupling in neuroscience
method: Review: statistical and modeling approaches to CFC and their pitfalls
key_finding: Apparent CFC can come from non-stationarity, non-sinusoidal shape or sharp transients, missing oscillations, or too-narrow amplitude filters; the phase-giving oscillation must exist
limitation: Review; gives no single fix
relevance_to_project: Core citation for gap 1: theta-gamma PAC during 40 Hz sound needs a real theta oscillation, a wide enough amplitude band, and waveform checks

title: Toward a proper estimation of phase–amplitude coupling in neural oscillations
method: Simulation study of PAC estimation choices (filter bandwidth, data length, measure)
key_finding: The amplitude filter must be wide enough to hold the side-bands at f_amp +/- f_phase, or coupling is lost or distorted
limitation: Rodent/hippocampal; not about driven responses
relevance_to_project: Concrete pitfall: a 38-42 Hz amplitude band cannot contain side-bands at 40 +/- (4-8) Hz, so theta modulation of the 40 Hz envelope is mostly filtered out before MI is computed
notes: Implication for the project pipeline is our inference from this paper, not tested by its authors

title: Misidentifications of specific forms of cross-frequency coupling: three warnings
method: Theory/simulation: three ways one CFC type gets mistaken for another
key_finding: Bicoherence reflects PAC, not phase-phase coupling; PAC can masquerade as amplitude-amplitude coupling and the reverse; non-sinusoidal signals produce spurious CFC
limitation: Conceptual
relevance_to_project: A 40 Hz driven response amplitude-modulated by a theta/delta rhythm, or theta-locked evoked responses, can show up as 'theta-gamma PAC' without a gamma oscillator nested in theta

title: Brain Oscillations and the Importance of Waveform Shape
method: Review of non-sinusoidal waveform shape (sharpness, rise-decay asymmetry) and how it breaks Fourier-based measures
key_finding: Non-sinusoidal oscillations create harmonics and spurious PAC; shape itself may carry physiological information
limitation: Review; tools (e.g., bycycle) not validated for driven responses
relevance_to_project: ds005048 used a 40 Hz RECTANGULAR amplitude modulation, which likely gives a non-sinusoidal driven response with harmonics; shape should be checked before any CFC is interpreted

title: Sharp edge artifacts and spurious coupling in EEG frequency comodulation measures
method: Short communication: sharp edges/abrupt voltage steps in EEG comodulation measures
key_finding: Abrupt voltage changes make broadband power that appears phase-locked to low frequencies (spurious coupling); detection checks proposed
limitation: Short paper, few quantitative guidelines
relevance_to_project: Stimulus on/off transitions (ON/OFF blocks) and click-like transients are exactly such sharp edges; PAC windows that span block boundaries are at risk

title: Neuronal Oscillations with Non-sinusoidal Morphology Produce Spurious Phase-to-Amplitude Coupling and Directionality
method: MEG lorazepam study + simulations of alpha-phase to beta/low-gamma amplitude coupling
data: Human MEG (placebo, 0.5, 1.5 mg lorazepam) + synthetic data
key_finding: Much of the observed alpha-to-beta/low-gamma coupling could be explained by non-sinusoidal alpha waveform (bicoherence at harmonics), with no cross-frequency directionality
limitation: Alpha band; resting/working-memory, not driven stimulation
relevance_to_project: Shows that 'coupling' up to ~45 Hz can be a harmonic artifact; relevant to reading theta/alpha-phase x 40 Hz PAC in older adults, whose rhythms change shape

title: Quantification of Phase-Amplitude Coupling in Neuronal Oscillations: Comparison of Phase-Locking Value, Mean Vector Length, Modulation Index, and Generalized-Linear-Modeling-Cross-Frequency-Coupling
method: Simulation comparison of PLV, MVL, MI, GLM-CFC with moderators (data length, SNR, sampling rate)
key_finding: All indices depend on data length, SNR and sampling rate near Nyquist; MI is the most robust for short, noisy epochs
limitation: Simulation only; no driven oscillations
relevance_to_project: In the project, 2 s windows give only 8-16 theta cycles and fs = 250 Hz, so MI bias and variance are large; surrogate normalization per window is needed

title: Phase-clustering bias in phase–amplitude cross-frequency coupling and its removal
method: Debiased PAC (dPAC): subtracts phase-clustering bias from mean-vector-length PAC
data: Simulations + macaque intracranial sleep, rat LFP
key_finding: A non-uniform phase distribution inflates or deflates PAC and can make it negative; dPAC corrects this
limitation: Corrects MVL-type measures; MI needs surrogates instead
relevance_to_project: Rhythmic stimulation locks phase to the stimulus (phase clustering), so this bias is expected to be larger during 40 Hz blocks than at rest

title: Theta‐gamma phase‐amplitude coupling explains the advantage of auditory plus visual gamma entrainment in Alzheimer’s therapy
method: Theta-gamma PAC during 40 Hz auditory, visual, and audio-visual stimulation (5 s on/5 s off, 60 trials)
data: Human EEG, n=10 cognitively healthy (per abstract)
key_finding: Reported markedly higher theta-gamma PAC for combined audio+visual 40 Hz than for either alone
limitation: Conference abstract (Alzheimer's & Dementia 17 S7); small n; healthy; no waveform/evoked-response controls reported
relevance_to_project: Closest prior use of theta-gamma PAC as a 40 Hz entrainment marker (same Sharif group as ds005048); its validity is unchecked against PAC02-PAC09
notes: Crossref-verified abstract DOI; no PMID (meeting abstract); conference abstract; not in PubMed

title: Transcranial Alternating Current Stimulation Alters Auditory Steady-State Oscillatory Rhythms and Their Cross-Frequency Couplings
method: Theta vs gamma vs sham tACS over temporal lobes during 40 Hz ASSR; ASSR power, phase locking and theta-gamma PAC
key_finding: Gamma tACS did not change the 40 Hz ASSR; theta tACS lowered 40 Hz power/phase locking and RAISED theta-gamma PAC
limitation: Healthy young adults; tACS artifacts; single session
relevance_to_project: Shows theta-gamma PAC during an ASSR can rise while the 40 Hz response itself weakens, so PAC and entrainment strength can move in opposite directions

title: Steady-State Visual Evoked Potentials Can Be Explained by Temporal Superposition of Transient Event-Related Responses
method: Synthesized SSVEPs by shifting and linearly adding rate-specific transient ERPs; compared with recorded SSVEPs
data: Human EEG, checkerboard reversal at several rates
key_finding: Synthetic SSRs closely matched recorded ones; no evidence of entrainment at the stimulation frequency
limitation: Visual, low rates, young adults; linear model fitted from ERPs recorded at each rate
relevance_to_project: A superposition null model any 40 Hz entrainment claim must beat; never applied to 40 Hz auditory stimulation in dementia

title: Modification of Brain Oscillations via Rhythmic Light Stimulation Provides Evidence for Entrainment but Not for Superposition of Event-Related Responses
method: Rhythmic vs jittered (arrhythmic) flicker across frequencies and intensities; phase coupling mapped against the Arnold tongue
data: Human EEG, visual flicker around individual alpha frequency
key_finding: Phase coupling grew with intensity and near the intrinsic frequency, matching an Arnold tongue; only inside the tongue did rhythmic differ from jittered stimulation; non-linear features
limitation: Alpha/visual only; young adults
relevance_to_project: Template for an Arnold-tongue test at gamma: vary 40 Hz rate and loudness, include a jittered control; not yet done for auditory 40 Hz in older adults

title: No Evidence for Entrainment: Endogenous Gamma Oscillations and Rhythmic Flicker Responses Coexist in Visual Cortex
method: MEG: rapid sinusoidal flicker up to 80 Hz combined with gratings that induce endogenous gamma; tests of phase/frequency entrainment
key_finding: No phase or frequency entrainment of endogenous gamma by flicker; the flicker response did not peak at the individual gamma frequency and fell with frequency; separate generators
limitation: Visual; young adults; frequencies >50 Hz were the main focus
relevance_to_project: Strongest human evidence that a gamma-rate driven response can coexist with, and be separate from, endogenous gamma; an auditory 40 Hz equivalent in older adults is missing

title: Human EEG responses to 1-100 Hz flicker: resonance phenomena in visual cortex and their potential correlation to cognitive phenomena
method: EEG flicker sweep 1-100 Hz in 1 Hz steps
key_finding: Steady-state responses at all rates up to at least 90 Hz, with resonance peaks near 10, 20, 40 and 80 Hz
limitation: Visual; young adults; resonance is not proof of entrainment
relevance_to_project: Frequency-sweep 'resonance' design; its auditory analog is the chirp ASSR (EVE10)

title: Generation of the 40-Hz auditory steady-state response (ASSR) explained using convolution
method: Deconvolution (CLAD) of ABR/MLR from jittered ~40 Hz clicks; ASSR synthesized by superposition
key_finding: 40 Hz ASSR explained by superposition of ABR wave V (~10%) and MLR Na-Pa and Nb-Pb (~45% each); the 40 Hz amplitude peak comes from Pb overlapping Pa
limitation: Young normal-hearing adults; click stimuli; linear model
relevance_to_project: Auditory superposition account: the 40 Hz 'resonance' can arise from overlapping middle-latency responses; untested in older adults, whose MLR latencies/amplitudes change

title: Auditory steady-state responses to 40-Hz click trains: Relationship to middle latency, gamma band and beta band responses studied with deconvolution
method: Deconvolved ABR/MLR and last-click responses used to predict 40 Hz click ASSRs, gamma-band and beta-band responses
key_finding: Superposition predicted the steady-state part of the ASSR but NOT its onset; click-rate adaptation matters
limitation: Young adults; clicks only
relevance_to_project: Suggests the onset/build-up period is where non-superposition dynamics could be tested, e.g., build-up time constants in dementia vs controls

title: Improved Transient Response Estimations in Predicting 40 Hz Auditory Steady-State Response Using Deconvolution Methods
method: Compared 40 Hz ASSR with ASSRs synthesized from 3 transient-AEP templates (5 Hz AEP, CLAD, MSAD deconvolution)
key_finding: The MSAD-derived template reproduced the 40 Hz ASSR with no significant difference in individuals, supporting linear superposition when the template is accurate
limitation: Young adults; template choice drives the conclusion
relevance_to_project: With EVE06/EVE07 and MEA08, the auditory 40 Hz evidence is split: steady part fits superposition, reset/onset show nonlinearity; none in older adults

title: Potentials evoked by chirp-modulated tones: a new technique to evaluate oscillatory activity in the auditory pathway
method: Chirp-modulated tones (AM rate sweeping) to map the response across modulation frequencies in one run
key_finding: Diagonal time-frequency band following the chirp; largest energy around 40-45 Hz (30-60 Hz), mainly from phase locking
limitation: Healthy adults; resonance-like profile does not separate entrainment from superposition
relevance_to_project: A fast per-person 'tuning curve' (resonance/Arnold-tongue proxy) that could be run in older adults/dementia; used in schizophrenia (Griskova-Bulanova 2020, 10.3390/brainsci11010022)

title: Rhythmic Entrainment Echoes in Auditory Perception
method: Behavioral 'entrainment echo' paradigm: target detection at varying delays after a rhythmic AM tone
key_finding: Strongest echoes after 6-8 Hz; best phases depended on the tonotopic match; echoes were not always consistent across experiments
limitation: Behavioral; low rates; not 40 Hz; no EEG
relevance_to_project: Post-offset persistence is a key entrainment criterion; no 40 Hz auditory echo test in older adults found

title: Test-Retest Reliability of the 40 Hz EEG Auditory Steady-State Response
method: Test-retest (~1 week) of the 40 Hz EEG ASSR; channel-level and dipole signal-space analysis; AM noise vs clicks
key_finding: ASSR correlated significantly between sessions; ITPC more reliable than evoked power; clicks more consistent than AM noise
limitation: Young healthy adults; correlations not ICCs; 1-week interval
relevance_to_project: Reliability reference for 40 Hz metrics; older/dementia reliability is almost unstudied (only IND05)

title: MEG and EEG demonstrate similar test-retest reliability of the 40 Hz auditory steady-state response
method: Test-retest (~1 week) of 40 Hz ASSR with MEG and EEG in the same people (source space)
key_finding: MEG ASSR significantly correlated between sessions; reliability similar for MEG and EEG; ITPC > evoked power; clicks > white noise
limitation: Small n; young adults
relevance_to_project: Suggests ITPC-type metrics are the most stable choice for per-person 40 Hz response indices

title: Test-retest reliability of time-frequency measures of auditory steady-state responses in patients with schizophrenia and healthy controls
method: Generalizability (G) coefficients for evoked power, total power, phase-locking factor and phase-locking angle at 20/30/40 Hz
data: Human EEG: 9 SZ + 9 HC (2 sessions) and 30 HC (2-3 sessions)
key_finding: G-coefficients good to excellent (>0.6) for most 40 Hz measures in both groups; 20 Hz less reliable
limitation: Small patient group; no older adults or dementia
relevance_to_project: Uses generalizability theory, which (like the hierarchical approach in NBM03) could be applied to 40 Hz responses in dementia datasets

title: MEG—measured auditory steady-state oscillations show high test–retest reliability: A sensor and source-space analysis
method: ICC of MEG ASSR (5 and 40 Hz AM tones) over 2 sessions, sensor + eLORETA source
key_finding: ITPC ICCs ~0.86-0.96, higher than spectral power change ICCs (~0.61-0.82)
limitation: n=13; young adults; task-embedded
relevance_to_project: Upper-bound reliability for 40 Hz ITPC under good conditions; compare with 19-channel clinical EEG at 250 Hz as in ds005048

title: Frequency optimisation for entrainment of gamma waves via sound stimulation in older adults
method: Auditory stimulation 37-45 Hz in 1 Hz steps; per-person optimal frequency
data: Human EEG, n=15 healthy adults aged 60-75
key_finding: No group effect of stimulation frequency, but each person's optimal frequency gave stronger entrainment than 40 Hz; also stronger connectivity
limitation: PREPRINT (Research Square), not peer-reviewed; small n; 'optimum' chosen and tested on the same data (circular unless cross-validated)
relevance_to_project: Directly relevant: frequency tuning in older adults for AUDITORY gamma; whether the individual optimum is stable across sessions is untested
notes: Crossref DOI verified (preprint); no PMID; preprint; not in PubMed

title: Center frequency as optimal frequency of visual stimulation for spreading entrained gamma rhythms to other target brain regions in cognitively normal older adults
method: Visual flicker at 32/34/36/38/40 Hz; individual center frequency (CF) from ERSP; gamma connectivity spread/strength/stability
data: Human EEG, n=32 cognitively normal older adults
key_finding: CF was 32 Hz (40.6%) or 34 Hz (28.1%) in about two-thirds; stimulating at CF gave broader, stronger, more stable connectivity
limitation: Visual; CF picked from the same session; no test-retest of CF
relevance_to_project: Individual 'tuning' in older adults is below 40 Hz for VISUAL; the auditory analog and CF stability are open
notes: Earlier study from same group: Park 2022, 10.1038/s41598-022-19464-2, PMID 36114215 (verified)

title: Personalized audiovisual gamma stimulation enhances neural connectivity and entrainment beyond fixed 40 Hz protocols
method: Compared 'conversation gamma frequency' (CGF), individual gamma frequency (IGF) and fixed 40 Hz stimulation; EEG connectivity and theta-gamma coupling
key_finding: CGF gave stronger activation/connectivity and more theta-gamma phase synchronization than 40 Hz; entrainment fell as CGF moved away from 40 Hz
limitation: Authors call it hypothesis-generating; PAC not checked for artifacts; sample unclear
relevance_to_project: Uses theta-gamma coupling as an entrainment readout, the practice gap 1 questions

title: Does brain ability to synchronize with 40 Hz auditory stimulation change with age?
method: Click-train 40 Hz ASSR; phase-locking index, evoked amplitude, total intensity; curve fitting against age
data: Human EEG, n=46 healthy males aged 20-58
key_finding: Phase-locking index and evoked amplitude fell linearly with age; total intensity did not
limitation: Males only; no one over 58; cross-sectional
relevance_to_project: Suggests phase-locked (evoked) and total power age differently, so the metric choice changes age conclusions

title: Aging Affects Neural Synchronization to Speech-Related Acoustic Modulations
method: 4, 20, 40, 80 Hz ASSRs in young, middle-aged and older adults with normal audiograms, screened for MCI
key_finding: Older adults: more theta-rate (4 Hz) synchronization, less 80 Hz, and loss of right-hemisphere dominance
limitation: Normal-hearing sample only; cross-sectional
relevance_to_project: Age changes the ASSR tuning profile, so older adults need age-appropriate reference values for 40 Hz responses

title: 40‐Hz oscillations underlying perceptual binding in young and older adults
method: MEG 40 Hz AM responses in quiet vs contralateral multitalker noise, young vs older adults
data: Human MEG, young and older adults
key_finding: Two components: a sensory component similar across ages, and a later component (200 ms amplitude/phase rebound) smaller in older adults and linked to speech-in-noise
limitation: MEG; small groups
relevance_to_project: The 40 Hz response in older adults is not one quantity; the 'higher-order' part shrinks with age

title: Gamma Frequency–Range Abnormalities to Auditory Stimulation in Schizophrenia
method: EEG ASSR to 20/30/40 Hz click trains in schizophrenia vs controls
data: Human EEG, schizophrenia vs controls (small groups, n~15 each)
key_finding: Reduced 40 Hz power (not lower rates), delayed phase synchronization onset and delayed desynchronization in schizophrenia
limitation: Small n; medicated patients
relevance_to_project: Start of the clinical ASSR field; its 'build-up/decay timing' metrics are rarely used in dementia 40 Hz studies

title: The 40-Hz Auditory Steady-State Response in Patients With Schizophrenia
method: Meta-analysis of 40 Hz ASSR in schizophrenia (1999-2016)
key_finding: 17/20 reported reductions; Hedges g -0.58 (power) and -0.46 (phase locking); stimulus/analysis choices did not moderate
limitation: Publication bias possible; medication confounds
relevance_to_project: Benchmark effect size: case-control 40 Hz differences are moderate, so a single-dataset dementia study (n~35) is underpowered for group or individual inferences

title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the auditory steady-state response in schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and autism spectrum disorder
method: Meta-analysis of 20/40/80 Hz ASSR in SZ, bipolar disorder, autism, relatives, clinical high risk
key_finding: 40 Hz power and ITPC reduced in SZ and BD; power reduced in ASD; reductions in first-degree relatives but not clinical-high-risk
limitation: Mostly cross-sectional; heterogeneous methods
relevance_to_project: Shows 40 Hz ASSR is not specific to one disorder, a caution for reading 40 Hz response changes in dementia as disease-specific

title: 40 Hz Steady-State Response in Human Auditory Cortex Is Shaped by Gabaergic Neuronal Inhibition
method: Placebo-controlled MEG pharmacology: lorazepam (GABA-A agonist) vs memantine (NMDA antagonist) vs placebo during 40 Hz ASSR
data: Human MEG, n=20 healthy adults (13 M, 7 F)
key_finding: Lorazepam increased 40 Hz ASSR amplitude in auditory cortex; no detectable memantine effect
limitation: Healthy young adults; low doses; single dose
relevance_to_project: Memantine is a common AD drug; this null suggests (not proves) memantine use is not a major 40 Hz ASSR confound, while benzodiazepines are; medication must be recorded
notes: Framed as a schizophrenia-biomarker mechanism study

title: Parvalbumin neurons and gamma rhythms enhance cortical circuit performance
method: Optogenetic drive of PV interneurons in mouse cortex; gamma induction and information transmission
key_finding: PV interneuron activity is sufficient to create gamma, and gamma improves signal transmission in cortical circuits
limitation: Mouse; optogenetic, not sensory, drive
relevance_to_project: Mechanism behind reading 40 Hz ASSR as a PV/E-I readout; see Cardin 2009 (10.1038/nature08002, PMID 19396156, verified) for the companion paper showing that driving fast-spiking cells creates gamma

title: Modeling GABA Alterations in Schizophrenia: A Link Between Impaired Inhibition and Altered Gamma and Beta Range Auditory Entrainment
method: Biophysical network model (E cells, fast/slow inhibition) of ASSR; prolonged GABA-A decay
data: Model fit to MEG ASSR from 12 SZ + 12 controls
key_finding: Longer inhibitory decay reproduced reduced 40 Hz and enhanced ~20 Hz responses to 40 Hz drive in schizophrenia
limitation: Tuned to schizophrenia; one cortical column; no aging/AD parameters
relevance_to_project: Makes a frequency-specific prediction (40 Hz loss with 20 Hz gain under 40 Hz drive) that could be checked in dementia EEG as a spectral signature
notes: PING/ING network family (Kopell lab)

title: The Role of Parvalbumin-positive Interneurons in Auditory Steady-State Response Deficits in Schizophrenia
method: Extension of MOD02 separating basket-cell vs chandelier-cell PV synapse changes
key_finding: Slowed basket-cell (not chandelier-cell) synapses best explain ASSR deficits
limitation: Model-only; schizophrenia-focused
relevance_to_project: Open, reusable ASSR model code base that could be refit to older-adult/dementia 40 Hz data

title: The beta component of gamma-band auditory steady-state responses in patients with schizophrenia
method: ASSR network model sweeping input strength under SZ-like changes (less GABA, longer GABA decay, NMDA hypofunction)
key_finding: Beta (20 Hz) power during 40 Hz drive appears only with longer GABA decay AND only in a limited range of input strength, through 'beat-skipping' (response to every other cycle)
limitation: Model-only; untested dependence on loudness in humans
relevance_to_project: FALSIFIABLE and testable: predicts a 20 Hz subharmonic during 40 Hz sound that depends on stimulus intensity; the dementia 40 Hz datasets could check for a 20 Hz subharmonic, though a loudness sweep is needed for a full test

title: Shaping Intrinsic Neural Oscillations with Periodic Stimulation
method: Network model of how periodic stimulation shapes intrinsic oscillations (entrainment, Arnold tongue, stochastic effects)
key_finding: Periodic stimulation entrains intrinsic oscillations within frequency-amplitude Arnold tongues; outcomes depend on the stimulation-to-intrinsic frequency mismatch and strength
limitation: Theory; aimed at tACS/TMS; not fit to sensory data
relevance_to_project: Gives the Arnold-tongue predictions (response width growing with intensity around the natural frequency) that separate entrainment from superposition

title: Neural masses and fields in dynamic causal modeling
method: Review of neural mass/field and conductance models used in dynamic causal modeling (DCM) of EEG/MEG/LFP
key_finding: Describes canonical-microcircuit and other population models that link spectra/ERPs to synaptic parameters
limitation: Models are complex; identifiability depends on data features
relevance_to_project: A DCM framework that could fit 40 Hz responses in older adults and dementia; no such application found

title: Computational Modeling of Electroencephalography and Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Paradigms Indicates a Consistent Loss of Pyramidal Cell Synaptic Gain in Schizophrenia
method: DCM (canonical microcircuit) fitted to resting EEG, MMN, 40 Hz ASSR, and resting fMRI
key_finding: All paradigms were best explained by more pyramidal-cell self-inhibition (less synaptic gain); auditory disinhibition predicted perceptual abnormality
limitation: Schizophrenia; model-comparison dependent
relevance_to_project: The only large-sample DCM of 40 Hz ASSR found; the same pipeline could be applied to dementia 40 Hz EEG to test E/I changes

title: Neurophysiologically-informed markers of individual variability and pharmacological manipulation of human cortical gamma
method: DCM of induced visual gamma across a large cohort; individual differences; tiagabine pharmacology validation
key_finding: Individual gamma differences were driven by superficial pyramidal-interneuron connections; more self-inhibition lowered gamma amplitude and raised peak frequency
limitation: Visual induced gamma, not ASSR
relevance_to_project: Shows DCM can explain individual gamma differences and be checked with a drug; a model of this type for 40 Hz auditory individual differences in older adults is missing

title: Generative Models of Cortical Oscillations: Neurobiological Implications of the Kuramoto Model
method: Review/tutorial on the Kuramoto coupled-phase-oscillator model and its neurobiological extensions
key_finding: Explains synchronization transitions, frequency locking and extensions (delays, networks) relevant to cortical rhythms
limitation: Abstract phase model; hard to map to EEG amplitude
relevance_to_project: A driven Kuramoto oscillator gives the simplest fittable entrainment model (locking range vs drive strength) for 40 Hz data

title: Understanding Heterogeneity in Clinical Cohorts Using Normative Models: Beyond Case-Control Studies
method: Normative modeling: Gaussian-process regression of brain measures on age/covariates; per-person deviation scores
key_finding: Case-control averages hide heterogeneity; per-person deviations from a normative model capture it
limitation: Needs large reference samples; mostly MRI so far
relevance_to_project: No normative model of 40 Hz ASSR/entrainment vs age exists (see AGE05); needed to judge whether a dementia patient's 40 Hz response is atypical
notes: Companion: Marquand 2019, 10.1038/s41380-019-0441-1, PMID 31201374 (verified)

title: Harmonized-Multinational qEEG norms (HarMNqEEG)
method: Harmonized multinational qEEG norms: Riemannian cross-spectral norms with site harmonization
data: Resting EEG, 9 countries, 12 devices (n in the thousands)
key_finding: Lifespan norms for EEG cross-spectra, with site effects modeled
limitation: Resting EEG only; no evoked or steady-state measures
relevance_to_project: Shows EEG normative modeling across sites is feasible; not yet extended to steady-state/40 Hz responses

title: Trial and error: A hierarchical modeling approach to test-retest reliability
method: Hierarchical (trial-level) Bayesian model that estimates test-retest reliability separately from trial noise
key_finding: Conventional ICCs on trial-averaged data underestimate reliability; hierarchical models recover it
limitation: Demonstrated for fMRI/behavior, not EEG steady-state data
relevance_to_project: Could estimate the reliability of per-window 40 Hz SNR/ITPC in datasets with few blocks per person (e.g., ds005048)

title: The reliability paradox: Why robust cognitive tasks do not produce reliable individual differences
method: Analysis of why robust group-level tasks give unreliable individual differences (reliability paradox)
key_finding: Low between-person variance, the thing that makes a task effect robust, lowers reliability of individual differences
limitation: Behavioral; does not cover EEG
relevance_to_project: A strong group 40 Hz response does not imply a stable per-person 40 Hz response; individual reliability has to be measured

title: Efficiently searching through large tACS parameter spaces using closed-loop Bayesian optimization
method: Closed-loop Bayesian optimization (Gaussian process) of tACS frequency/phase using participant judgements
key_finding: Found per-person stimulation parameters in about 5 minutes within a large parameter space
limitation: Behavioral objective (phosphenes); not EEG entrainment
relevance_to_project: Could tune per-person auditory gamma frequency/intensity with an EEG objective (e.g., 40 Hz SNR), with safeguards against circular selection
notes: Conceptual framework: Lorenz 2017 'Neuroadaptive Bayesian optimization', 10.1016/j.tics.2017.01.006, PMID 28236531 (verified)

title: Auditory Closed-Loop Stimulation of the Sleep Slow Oscillation Enhances Memory
method: Closed-loop auditory stimulation timed to slow-oscillation up-states during sleep
key_finding: In-phase clicks enhanced slow oscillations, spindles and declarative memory; out-of-phase clicks did not
limitation: Sleep slow oscillations; young adults
relevance_to_project: Proves phase-dependent closed-loop AUDITORY stimulation works; 40 Hz stimulation has not been gated by ongoing theta/alpha phase or state

title: Phase-locked loop for precisely timed acoustic stimulation during sleep
method: Phase-locked loop (PLL) that tracks EEG and times acoustic stimuli during slow-wave sleep
key_finding: A simple, predictive PLL delivered sound at a chosen slow-wave phase and boosted slow-wave activity
limitation: Sleep only
relevance_to_project: Engineering template for real-time phase tracking in a closed-loop 40 Hz scheduler

title: A state space modeling approach to real-time phase estimation
method: State-space oscillator model with Kalman filtering for real-time phase estimation (with credible intervals)
key_finding: Beats band-pass/Hilbert phase estimation for broadband, non-stationary rhythms and gives phase uncertainty
limitation: Tested on low-frequency rhythms; compute cost for multi-oscillator fits
relevance_to_project: Enables uncertainty-aware theta/alpha phase gating of 40 Hz stimulation; related model: Matsuda & Komaki 2017, 10.1162/NECO_a_00916, PMID 27870609 (verified)

title: ComBat models for harmonization of resting-state EEG features in multisite studies
method: Four ComBat variants (neuroCombat, neuroHarmonize, OPNested-GMM, HarmonizR) for resting EEG features
data: Resting EEG, n=374 from 5 datasets, young and old adults
key_finding: All reduced batch effects; HarmonizR and OPNested-GMM best; age relations kept and effect sizes larger after harmonization
limitation: Resting spectral features only; sensor space
relevance_to_project: Needed to pool 40 Hz response features across datasets (different amplifiers, montages, fs); not yet done for steady-state data
notes: Original ComBat: Johnson 2007, 10.1093/biostatistics/kxj037, PMID 16632515 (verified)

title: Transfer Learning: A Riemannian Geometry Framework With Applications to Brain–Computer Interfaces
method: Riemannian-geometry transfer learning (re-centering covariance matrices) across sessions/subjects
key_finding: Re-centering covariances allows cross-session/cross-subject transfer with little calibration
limitation: Built for BCI classification, not biomarkers
relevance_to_project: A domain-adaptation route for moving 40 Hz response models between datasets or devices

title: EEGManyPipelines: A Large-scale, Grassroots Multi-analyst Study of Electroencephalography Analysis Practices in the Wild
method: Multi-analyst study: 168 teams analyzed the same EEG dataset for the same hypotheses
key_finding: Documents large differences in analysis pipelines and results (project overview paper)
limitation: Overview; hypotheses not about steady-state responses
relevance_to_project: Supports pre-registered, multiverse checks of 40 Hz entrainment metrics (reference, filters, window, metric) in a small single dataset

title: 40Hz Auditory Entrainment
method: OpenNeuro BIDS EEG dataset: 40 Hz auditory entrainment (5 kHz carrier, 40 Hz rectangular AM), stimulation vs rest blocks
data: 35 older adults (local participants.tsv: 10 normal, 6 MCI, 16 mild AD, 1 moderate AD, 2 unlabelled; age 54-89), 19-ch EEG, fs 250 Hz
key_finding: Open data for 40 Hz AUDITORY stimulation in dementia, with MMSE
limitation: One session per participant; no alternative frequency or jittered control; 250 Hz fs limits harmonic analysis
relevance_to_project: Main data source; supports within-session split-half reliability but not test-retest
notes: DataCite DOI verified (not Crossref-registered); license CC0

title: High-density EEG of auditory steady-state responses during stimulation of basal forebrain parvalbumin neurons
method: Data descriptor: high-density (36-ch) mouse EEG ASSRs to 10/20/30/40/50 Hz clicks, with/without optogenetic basal-forebrain PV stimulation
key_finding: Raw epochs + Python tutorials; includes a coupled-oscillator perturbation simulation
limitation: Mouse; anesthesia/implant differences from humans
relevance_to_project: Open multi-rate ASSR data for testing resonance/Arnold-tongue analyses and oscillator vs superposition models across species
notes: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.3949519 (DataCite verified)
